Policy Name: Cigna ACDF (CMM-601: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion)
Referred Sections: CMM-601.9: Non-Indications > Experimental, Investigational, or Unproven (EIU)
Non-Indications: Anterior cervical discectomy/corpectomy and fusion performed without meeting the criteria in the General Guidelines when applicable for urgent/emergent conditions) and the criteria in the applicable procedure-specific section(s) ( initial fusion , corpectomy , repeat fusion , adjacent segment disease , or fusion following failed disc arthroplasty ) is considered not medically necessary .

Anterior cervical discectomy/corpectomy and fusion performed for ANY other reason is considered not medically necessary including, but not limited to, performed for EITHER of the following conditions:
chronic non-specific neck or arm pain of unknown etiology
cervical degenerative disc disease without radiculopathy or myelopathy
Anterior cervical discectomy/corpectomy performed alone (i.e., performed without a cervical fusion)

Anterior cervical osteotomy or vertebral column resection (VCR) performed without meeting the criteria in the General Guidelines section (when applicable for urgent/ emergent conditions) and the criteria in CMM-601.2 Osteotomy is considered not medically necessary .
Important criteria & exceptions: Anterior endoscopic cervical disc/nerve root decompression is considered experimental, investigational, or unproven , including ANY of the following procedures:
anterior endoscopic cervical decompression with microforaminotomy (e.g., Jho procedure)
anterior endoscopic cervical disc decompression (e.g., Cervical Deuk Laser Disc Repair)
Documentation required: Operative report from prior cervical surgery
Cervical MRI/CT radiology reports showing neural compression
Physical therapy and pharmacy records documenting >= 6 weeks of conservative care
